description: Dark stone webbed in gold thorns around a green heart, off a Thornstag. Flowers die near it, indoors.
lore: It lives outside, on the sill, in a stone box. A dealer who forgets loses whatever was in the room with it — cut flowers in one night, then the herbs strung over the stove, then the pot by the window — and the standing test for a true one is exactly that and nothing cleverer. A cut stem laid beside it until morning. Sellers hand you the stem themselves. A proof that costs a flower is a cheap proof.

Dark, gold-webbed, no trouble at all to grade. Whatever comes at you comes away torn and slower, and does not get its pace back while the fight lasts. [[monsters/corrupt_stag|The stag]] browses a plot down to dirt and the plot stays dirt, that year and after. One fact to a stone, pressed until it is nearly a mineral, and the fact in this one is about things not coming back.

The part worth looking at costs nothing extra. Turn it to the light and the middle of it is green — a plain grass-green heart, the same green as the stone of any leaf-eating animal on the same bench, and every thorn in the thing worked outside it. Something in that wood used to browse and mind its own business. There is no account anywhere of a Thornstag that did not read as a hole cut out of the dark: not in [[lore/the_chronicle|the Chronicle]], not from the oldest teller anybody has been able to produce. A hundred and sixty gold, and the green middle is the entire evidence, and it cannot decay, and it cannot be forgotten, and nothing further can be added to it.
gm_notes: Jehanne's bellflower plot is the creature record's story and is untouched here. This one is the batch's clearest 'a stone is evidence' record: the green heart is straight off the sprite and it is the only surviving witness that a Thornstag was ever an ordinary browsing animal — a fact nobody in a country made of remembering remembers. Sad before evil; the stone reads as a wound that closed wrong, not as malice. Leaves room for a later beat about what happened to it without committing to one.
